title: PrIDE: Achieving Secure Rowhammer Mitigation with Low-Cost In-DRAM Trackers
problem: Existing low-cost in-DRAM trackers with 1-30 entries can be broken within minutes by adversarial access patterns, while provably secure alternatives require thousands of entries, creating a gap between practical and secure solutions.
motivation: Rowhammer attacks pose a critical security threat to DRAM, requiring efficient mitigation that is both practical and provably secure.
method: PrIDE tracks memory accesses using a first-in-first-out queue (a simple FIFO buffer), but makes random decisions about which rows to track and when to remove them, so these choices don't depend on an attacker's access pattern. This randomness prevents an attacker from gaming the tracker by accessing memory in a strategic sequence to avoid detection. The researchers developed a mathematical formula to calculate how long an attacker would need to break any given security threshold, and showed the design works alongside refresh-rate management to enable lower attack thresholds (400 accesses instead of 1.9K) with just 1.6% slowdown.
key_novelty: Making random decisions about which rows to track instead of using predictable rules prevents attackers from evading the tracker, providing proven security guarantees even with a small, low-cost buffer.
contributions: First low-cost in-DRAM tracker achieving provably secure Rowhammer mitigation
Novel insight that policy decisions must be independent of access patterns to prevent evasion attacks
Probabilistic FIFO design tolerating 1.9K thresholds with only 4 entries and 10 bytes of storage
Co-design with RFM extending security to 400 thresholds with 1.6% slowdown

metrics.other: 10,000+ year time-to-failure per bank, 1.6% slowdown with RFM

primary_theme: Secure low-cost rowhammer mitigation via probabilistic tracking
